samples.summary: The chip's new "turn on offline saving" CTA reaches the share-link route, where durability is permanently refused
samples.evidence: `SharedHeaderStatus` renders `SyncStatusChip` for every editor-role share-link visitor (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-header-status.tsx:26), inside the layout's `DocumentProvider` and therefore inside the `NonDurableScope` the diff adds at packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:1016. The chip's new offer is gated only on `stranded && supportsClientKey() && !offlineEnabled` (packages/frontend/src/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.tsx:83) — it never consults `useDurabilityPermitted()`, which the same change makes available. So a share-link visitor who strands work now gets a clickable "Not saved" button and a toast action "Turn on for later documents" that enables a device-wide preference; for the document in front of them it can never apply (NonDurableScope), and for an anonymous visitor — the common case on `/shared/:token`, where `fetchMeOptional` answers `null` — it can never apply to anything, since `useDurableDocument` refuses without a `userId`. `sync-status-tooltip.ts` deliberately suppresses the `not-permitted` diagnosis on exactly the grounds that "a share link was never going to be saved to the visitor's device", which the offer then contradicts. The fix belongs on the new code: fold `useDurabilityPermitted()` (and an identity check) into `offerOffline`.

samples.summary: design-sandbox renders the Settings page as a scene but does not define the new `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` global the page now depends on
samples.evidence: `packages/design-sandbox/scenes.config.json:218` declares the `settings-personal` scene as `packages/frontend/src/app/settings/page.tsx`, and the sandbox aliases `@` → `packages/frontend/src` (packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts:212). The diff makes that page import `@/lib/yorkie-capabilities`, whose `supportsClientKey()` reads the build-time global `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` — added only to `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts`. The sandbox's `define` block (packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts:186-190) supplies `process.env` and `__APP_VERSION__` only, and its own comment two lines above states that scene source "reaches `process.env` shims and `__APP_VERSION__`, and an undefined global is a hard failure rather than a degraded render". Here the `typeof` guard means it degrades rather than throws: the sandbox resolves `0.0.0`, so the new Offline section will never render in the scene even after `@yorkie-js/react` is bumped past `MinClientKeyVersion`, leaving the design scene permanently out of step with the shipped page. Fix: mirror the `define` entry in the sandbox config.

samples.summary: Offline housekeeping runs for every authenticated session with no capability or preference gate, adding a full `GET /documents` and an IndexedDB database on builds where nothing can ever be stored
samples.evidence: `PrivateRoute` mounts `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` unconditionally (packages/frontend/src/PrivateRoute.tsx:35). `OfflineRuntime`'s effect (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:62-160) checks neither `supportsClientKey()` nor `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`: on every authenticated app load it writes `wafflebase-offline-user` to localStorage, constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore` (creating the `wafflebase-offline` IndexedDB database), runs `collectStale()`, and issues `fetchDocuments()` — which is `GET /documents`, the whole cross-workspace listing (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:180-195), outside React Query so it is not shared with or deduped against the document-list query. This branch pins `@yorkie-js/react` to `0.7.22` (packages/frontend/package.json:66), below `MinClientKeyVersion`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false and nothing is ever written to that store — the request, the database and the stored user id are pure cost for 100% of signed-in users today. Gating the effect on `supportsClientKey()` would make the dark-launch actually dark.
